original_question: Which overcomplete Gabor frames {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z} admit at least one ordering {f_k}_{k in I} for which there exists a bounded linear operator T and a vector phi with {f_k}_{k in I}={T^k phi}_{k in I}? Equivalently, what conditions on the lattice parameters a,b>0 and the window g in L^2(R) determine whether some ordering of the frame can be generated by iterating a bounded operator?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1, as reformulated for overcomplete Gabor frames in Proposition 1.2 and partially tested by Theorem 1.3.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s central objects and mechanism: overcomplete Gabor frames in L^2(R), the dependence on how the doubly indexed family is ordered, and the question of whether such an ordering can be realized as a bounded-operator orbit {T^k phi}. It also correctly keeps the problem at the level of bounded linear operators on L^2(R), which is exactly the operator-theoretic issue emphasized in the introduction.
missing_details: The paper formulates the issue as a yes/no existence problem, not as a full classification of all triples (a,b,g).
The official formulation is about choosing an appropriate ordering of the Gabor frame elements and reindexing them by Z, so that the ordered family is a two-sided orbit {T^k phi}_{k in Z}.
The ambient space should be stated explicitly as L^2(R), and T should be a bounded linear operator L^2(R) -> L^2(R).
The ordered family must be an ordering of the original doubly indexed set {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z}, i.e. a bijective reindexing rather than an arbitrary new sequence.
The term "overcomplete" should be made stand-alone: the Gabor system is assumed to be a frame for L^2(R) but not a Riesz basis.
Your draft broadens the paper’s intent from existence/nonexistence to a parameter classification in terms of a,b,g; the paper does not ask for such a classification.
The paper’s nearby context uses Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 to sharpen the formulation and record partial evidence/obstructions, so the refined question should stay close to that narrower scope.
refined_question: Does there exist an overcomplete Gabor frame {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z} for L^2(R) such that, after a suitable bijective ordering of its elements by Z, the ordered frame can be written in the form {T^k phi}_{k in Z} for some bounded linear operator T:L^2(R)->L^2(R) and some phi in L^2(R)?
justification: The draft is very close in theme, but the paper’s actual target is narrower. In the introduction, the authors formulate the issue as an existence/nonexistence question about whether any overcomplete Gabor frame admits an ordering that is a bounded-operator orbit; they do not ask for a complete characterization of all lattice parameters and windows. Proposition 1.2 gives the precise Gabor-frame reformulation of the conjectural question, and Theorem 1.3 supplies the paper’s partial result/obstruction for a special setup. So the sharpest paper-faithful rewrite is the yes/no existence question above, with explicit two-sided indexing by Z and explicit reindexing of the Gabor family.
